```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(depprep)
```

Samples taken close together resemble each other. When many variables are measured at
the same sites, part of the correlation between two variables comes only from both
following the same large-scale pattern of space. `depprep` removes that part and keeps
the rest, so that PCA, MDS, k-means or SOM see the association between the variables
rather than the map of the samples.

## Data with known truth

We simulate 200 sites and ten variables: four follow a broad field, three a fine field,
three have no spatial dependence. Their residual components are correlated in blocks
(0.5 within the broad and within the fine variables, 0 between them): that is the
association we want to recover.

```{r simulate}
g <- sim_groups(sim_group("broad", 4, "exponential", range = 0.5),
                sim_group("fine", 3, "exponential", range = 0.15),
                sim_group("none", 3, "none"))
sim <- sim_spatial(200, g, R_true = make_R_true(g, "blocks", within = 0.5, between = 0), seed = 1)
dim(sim$X)
```

With your own data, replace `sim` by the data matrix and give the coordinates
(`coords`, projected, for example in km) to every function.

## 1. Diagnose each variable alone

The diagnosis looks at one variable at a time (Moran's I, correlogram, variogram), never
at the correlations between variables, which are what we want to estimate.

```{r diagnose}
sig <- diagnose_variables(sim, nsim = 99)
sig[, c("variable", "dependence_p", "range", "nugget_ratio")]
```

## 2. Group the variables by regime

Variables with similar signatures form a group; each group will share one basis.

```{r group}
gr <- group_regimes(sig)
gr[, c("variable", "type", "group")]
```

## 3. Correct

```{r correct}
cr <- correct(sim, gr)
cr
```

`cr$R` is the corrected correlation matrix (for PCA). `cr$X` is the corrected data
(for MDS, k-means, SOM), where each variable is corrected with a basis selected on that
variable alone, which keeps the classes.

Because the data are simulated, we can compare both matrices with the true
correlation of the residual components:

```{r compare}
err <- function(R) sqrt(mean((R - sim$R_true)[upper.tri(R)]^2))
c(raw = err(cor(sim$X)), corrected = err(cr$R))
```

## 4. Verify

```{r verify}
v <- verify(cr, sim, nperm = 49)
v
```

The table `v$variables` says, for each variable, how much was removed, its
autocorrelation before and after and whether structure is left; `v$lisa` gives the local
Moran's I of each corrected variable, to see where structure is left. The Q3 warning
says whether much of the association between variables lived at the scale of the
basis: if the classes you look for could be regions, the correction would remove them.

```{r lisa}
head(v$variables[, c("variable", "removed", "autocor_before", "autocor_after", "lisa_share")])
```

## 5. Your own structures

If you know the process (here, say, that only the broad trend matters, or that the
neighbourhood graph should be chosen), give a menu; the parameters are still searched
with the same tests:

```{r menu}
m <- basis_menu(term_trend(), term_mem(W = "auto"))
cr_m <- correct(sim, gr, menu = m, scope = "groups")
vapply(cr_m$bases, function(b) attr(b, "W"), "")
```

## 6. A report for the user

```{r report, eval = FALSE}
report_correction(cr, sim, v, file = "depprep_report.html")
```

The same steps are available point and click with `run_app()`.
